newsitem.title: USA: Collective falls after merger news.
newsitem.headline: Collective falls after merger news.

text.p: Shares of Egg Harbor City, N.J.-based Collective Bancorp fell 1-1/2 to 40-1/2 in early trading after news the company was being acquired by Summit Bancorp, New Jersey's biggest bank.

Analyst Elizabeth Summers of Ryan, Beck & Co said the decline in Collective may have been because some investors were assuming the company would be sold for a higher price. She said Summit was paying 2.3 times Collective's book value of $18.45 per share, which is believed to be the highest multiple to book value that has ever been paid for a thrift in New Jersey.
"I view this deal as very positive for Collective," Summers said.

Collective shareholders will receive 0.895 Summit share for each Collective share. Based on Summit's closing price Thursday, the transaction valued Collective at $42.51 per share or $867 million. Summit was off 1/4 to 47-1/4 Friday morning.

Summers said trading also reflected arbitrage activity and the fact the deal is not expected to close until the third quarter of 1997. She said it is typical for the stock of a target company to trade initially at a 10-15 percent discount.
